note: THE ANCHOR CONTRACT (cinatra#2826, epic #2784 S9m) — the drift alarm between the design pin, the executable DOM expectations and the anchors a capture is graded against. `digest` is a sha256 over exactly three inputs: the acceptance manifest's `specCommit` (read from the manifest, never from here — the copy below is a readable mirror), the `domExpectations` recorded below, and the capture requirement anchors recomputed live from scripts/audit/lib/chat-hitl-capture-recorder.mjs. Moving the design pin therefore invalidates the digest by itself, and so does renaming an anchor, adding a host cell, weakening an observation or changing what a capture must observe. The only way back is an explicit re-ratification: re-examine the anchors against the drawing at the new pin and record the new digest by hand. `node scripts/audit/chat-hitl-acceptance-gate.mjs --print-anchor-digest` prints the recomputed value; nothing writes it, because a digest a script refreshes on its own alarms about nothing. The other half of the binding is src/lib/lifecycle/__tests__/anchor-contract-binding.test.ts, which asserts these `domExpectations` deep-equal the executable ones — so the code cannot move without this file, and this file cannot move without the digest. RE-RATIFIED 2026-08-22 (cinatra#2893): the pin moved to the §V addition drawing the ZERO-CHIP SETTLED READING, and the anchors were re-examined against it rather than refreshed. The two DOM expectation halves are UNCHANGED and that is the finding, not an omission — `carriage` names the ONE owner that draws each kind and the root declarations it is ruled by, and `hostParity` names which host draws each kind and how; the addition gives the recommendation card a new FACE for one state, not a new owner, a new root declaration or a new host. The capture requirements are unchanged for the same reason: a zero-chip settled capture is a `recommendation_hold` in the `decided` state, and the decided contract already asks for the state declaration inside the card root and the absence of every per-chip control — which is exactly what the outcome panel draws. The digest moved on the pin alone, which is the alarm working as designed. RE-RATIFIED AGAIN 2026-08-22 (cinatra#2788, S9d): the design pin did NOT move — what moved is the CAPTURE REQUIREMENT for `trigger_schedule_proposal`, and it moved because the card now exists to be graded. The placeholder-era requirement named `[data-action]`, written before any of §VI was drawn, and that selector matches BOTH the proposal's decision floor and the settled chrome's two operations. Re-examined against the drawing at the pin: §VI's decision floor is `Adjust · Confirm` and nothing else — "this floor is the only new drawing in this section" — while `Cancel trigger` and `Release now` are the SETTLED trigger's own controls, which §VI draws on a card that has already been decided ("two quiet right-aligned controls"). So the requirement is now the FLOOR'S OWN UNION — one selector list naming both floor actions: an undecided capture owes at least one control on it, a decided one owes none. It is a union rather than two members because §VI's floor draws different controls in different phases (Adjust · Confirm live, Adjust alone once expired, §7 step 5), and the audit tier reads a multi-member group as "every member present" — true of the chip row, which renders all three unconditionally, and false here. Under the old wording a truthful settled capture of this kind was refused for showing the controls the drawing gives it, and a pending one could have been answered by a control that decides nothing. The two DOM expectation halves are unchanged: the card's owner, its root declarations and its hosts are what S9d's own gate rows record, and none of them moved with this re-examination.
